claims.text: The news industry sells the one thing whose price is going to zero, the article, and throws away the one thing nobody else has, the evidence the article was made from.
claims.quote: The news industry sells the one thing whose price is going to zero, the article, and throws away the one thing nobody else has, the evidence the article was made from.

claims.text: Under advertising the reader is the product and the content is bait; under a subscription the reader is the hostage and the content the excuse; neither pays for what the reader came for.
claims.quote: Advertising sells the reader to somebody else, so the reader is the product and the content is bait.

claims.text: Somebody in the author's household pays roughly £50 a month across news subscriptions and reads, in a good month, a tenth of what that buys.
claims.quote: pays roughly £50 a month across news subscriptions and reads, in a good month, a tenth of what that buys

value.unit: GBP a month on news subscriptions, a tenth read

claims.text: The 2026 Reuters Institute data has trust in news at 37%, the lowest since 2015, and 42% of people sometimes or often avoiding the news.
claims.quote: the lowest since it was first measured in 2015, and 42% of people saying they sometimes or often avoid the news altogether

claims.text: The objective is a commercial model that rewards investigative journalism: evidenced reporting drives usage, usage drives revenue that depends on neither search nor renewals, and revenue funds more reporting.
claims.quote: The objective is a commercial model that rewards investigative journalism.

claims.text: Chartbeat data across more than 2,500 sites has organic Google search traffic to publishers down 33% globally in the year to November 2025, and 38% in the United States.
claims.quote: organic Google search traffic to publishers down 33% globally in the year to November 2025, and 38% in the United States

value.unit: % fall in organic Google search traffic to publishers

claims.text: Cloudflare began blocking AI crawlers by default in July 2025 with HTTP 402, and from 15 September 2026 blocks any crawler that will not say whether it is search, training or an agent.
claims.quote: from 15 September 2026 any crawler that will not say whether it is search, training or an agent is blocked

claims.text: Cloudflare's customers send more than a billion 402 responses a day.
claims.quote: more than a billion 402s a day

value.unit: 402 responses a day from Cloudflare customers

claims.text: Across the twenty countries the Reuters Institute has tracked for a decade, 17% pay for online news, down from 18%, and the 2026 report calls 10% to 20% a ceiling in most markets.
claims.quote: 17% pay for online news, down from 18%

value.unit: % who pay for online news across twenty countries

claims.text: Of those who do not pay, 71% told the 2025 survey that nothing on offer would persuade them, 65% in the UK.
claims.quote: 71% told the 2025 survey that nothing on offer would persuade them, 65% in the UK

claims.text: The UK's Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act subscription regime, with renewal reminders and easy cancellation and fines up to 10% of turnover, was brought forward on 10 August 2026 to 1 January 2027.
claims.quote: On 10 August 2026 the government brought it forward to 1 January 2027

claims.text: James Ball's case against paying per article: a $100 subscription lost is 500 micropayments, a newspaper is a bundle, value is known only after reading, and publishers will not cooperate.
claims.quote: A $100 subscription lost is 500 micropayments to replace.

claims.text: Blendle had more than a million users, of whom 150,000 ever paid, and pivoted to subscriptions in 2019.
claims.quote: Blendle, which had more than a million users, of whom 150,000 ever paid, and pivoted to subscriptions in 2019

claims.text: Three buyers stand at the till today, the reader who wants one thing, the firm that has to forward it, and the agent paying per query, and none of them wants the article.
claims.quote: None of the three wants the article.

claims.text: Dominic Young of Axate: there are more people in the market willing to pay than willing to subscribe, and the one-off option barely exists.
claims.quote: There are more people in the market willing to pay than willing to subscribe.

claims.text: The agent has no anxiety and no brain cycles to conserve; it has a wallet, which makes the mental transaction cost argument beside the point because the transaction is not mental.
claims.quote: It has no anxiety and no brain cycles to conserve. It has a wallet.

claims.text: The story is a graph of claims, evidence, sources, raw materials, analysis and drafts; the article is one projection of it, a walk through the graph for one audience at one moment.
claims.quote: the story is a graph; the article is a projection.

claims.text: The dataset is worth more than the article: the words any model can regenerate in a second, the frozen sources and the chain from claim to bytes nobody else has.
claims.quote: The dataset is worth more than the article.

claims.text: Meaning comes from connectivity: a node means nothing on its own, every edge is a verb with a named inverse, and an edge with no verb is banned.
claims.quote: a node means nothing on its own; what it is arrives through its edges.

claims.text: The graph is fractal: zoom into any node and you enter a new world with its own node types, verbs and vocabulary, joined to the one you left by a single named edge.
claims.quote: Zoom into any node and you enter a new world with its own node types, its own verbs and its own vocabulary

claims.text: A correction propagates instead of being republished: mark one node superseded and every path that rested on it becomes a query rather than an archaeology project.
claims.quote: A correction propagates instead of being republished.

claims.text: Evidence is frozen bytes with a SHA-256 hash; provenance is the path from a claim through named edges to that evidence, a statement of what the claim rests on, not that it is true; trust is earned when provenance holds over time.
claims.quote: Provenance is not a statement that the claim is true. It is a statement of what the claim rests on

claims.text: The Regulation Graph ends every chain in a hash of the retrieved bytes, and so does the Portugal newsroom, for 88 sources today.
claims.quote: ends every chain in a hash of the retrieved bytes for exactly this reason, and so does the Portugal newsroom, for 88 sources today

value.unit: sources frozen and hashed by the Portugal newsroom

claims.text: The newsroom design's worked story, on the EU AI Act in Portugal, took 12 sources, two expert validations, four drafts, £8.40 and six hours twenty-three minutes of compute, and zero human hours.
claims.quote: 12 sources, two expert validations, four drafts, £8.40 and six hours twenty-three minutes of compute, and zero human hours

value.unit: GBP of compute for the worked story

claims.text: The worked story is a design example rather than a production ledger, and the page says so.
claims.quote: It is a worked design example rather than a production ledger, and the page says so.

claims.text: Five things to sell from one graph: the public article free as the door, the licensed article, the evidence vault, the customised projection, and the verification API.
claims.quote: One graph, five projections, and the free one is the door.

claims.text: The evidence vault is the tier nobody sells today and the one with the highest value, because its buyers are analysts, lawyers, academics, regulators and other newsrooms, who already pay for data.
claims.quote: This is the tier nobody sells today and the one with the highest value, because its buyers are not readers.

claims.text: The verification API answers a company or an agent on the record, with the chain attached and a warranty, as trust as a service; selling trust makes the seller a target, which is why the market pays.
claims.quote: selling trust makes the seller a target

claims.text: The proposed split pays 60% to the original researcher, 25% to the organisation holding the data, 10% to the journalist and 5% to the outlet, where today nearly all of it stops at the outlet.
claims.quote: 60% to the original researcher whose work the story rests on, 25% to the organisation that holds the data, 10% to the journalist who synthesised it and 5% to the outlet

value.unit: % of revenue to the original researcher

claims.text: The x402 protocol moved under the Linux Foundation in April 2026, settles in about 200 milliseconds, charges no protocol fee, and carried roughly 169 million transactions in its first year.
claims.quote: settles in about 200 milliseconds, charges no protocol fee, and carried roughly 169 million transactions in its first year

value.unit: x402 transactions in its first year

claims.text: Nothing on sgit.ai is wired to any of those rails today: no fact-creator payment, no per-query billing and no trust-as-a-service product runs anywhere.
claims.quote: Nothing on sgit.ai is wired to any of those rails today

claims.text: The entire published estate, thirty-one vaults, is 2,662 files and 295 MB of object storage with nothing running between requests, so a story vault costs what its files cost.
claims.quote: thirty-one vaults, is 2,662 files and 295 MB of object storage with nothing running between requests

value.unit: vaults in the published estate, 295 MB

claims.text: The Portuguese newsroom has ninety-two source files frozen and SHA-256 verified, 312 nodes and 942 edges extracted, five articles published, and a six-stage pipeline whose last stage no agent can move.
claims.quote: Ninety-two source files frozen and SHA-256 verified, 312 nodes and 942 edges extracted from them, five articles published

value.unit: source files frozen in the Portuguese newsroom

claims.text: Eight things a publisher could start this quarter, beginning with storing the story as a graph from the first day of reporting and freezing and hashing every source.
claims.quote: Store the story as a graph from the first day of reporting.

claims.text: The Regulation Graph parses the EU AI Act from the official Formex XML, hash-verified against the bytes it came from: the evidence layer of a story vault, done for a law.
claims.quote: The EU AI Act parsed from the official Formex XML, hash-verified against the bytes it came from
